cable-reverse-fly.description: A standing cable fly that keeps tension on the rear shoulders as the arms sweep outward.
instructions: Set both pulleys near shoulder height, take the opposite handles, and stand centered with arms crossed in front.
With soft elbows, sweep both arms out and back until they align with your torso.
Pause with the handles spread, then guide them across the front under control.
Keep your chest still and avoid turning the fly into a row by bending the elbows further.

reverse-pec-deck.description: A machine-supported reverse fly that isolates the rear shoulders along a fixed path.
instructions: Face the pad, set the handles at shoulder level, and brace your chest against the support.
Press the handles apart in a wide arc while keeping a slight, steady bend in your elbows.
Finish when your upper arms reach the line of your torso, then let the handles return slowly.
Keep your shoulders down and your chest on the pad instead of leaning back for momentum.

incline-dumbbell-reverse-fly.description: A chest-supported dumbbell fly that targets the rear shoulders without relying on torso momentum.
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand and palms facing inward.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides in a broad arc, keeping the elbows softly bent.
Stop as the upper arms approach torso level, then lower the dumbbells beneath the bench with control.
Keep your chest planted and neck neutral so the rear shoulders, not a body swing, drive the lift.

seated-dumbbell-shoulder-press.description: A bench-supported overhead press for the shoulders using independently moving dumbbells.
instructions: Sit against an upright bench and hold the dumbbells beside your shoulders with forearms vertical.
Press both dumbbells upward, bringing them slightly inward as your elbows straighten.
Finish overhead without striking the weights together, then lower them to shoulder level slowly.
Keep your back against the pad and wrists stacked over your elbows throughout the press.

standing-dumbbell-shoulder-press.description: A standing dumbbell press that trains the shoulders while the trunk stabilizes the overhead path.
instructions: Stand with feet firmly planted and hold the dumbbells at shoulder height with forearms upright.
Brace your trunk and press the dumbbells overhead without using a knee dip or leg drive.
Reach a balanced overhead position, then lower both weights smoothly to the shoulders.
Keep your ribs stacked over your pelvis and do not lean back to clear the dumbbells.

barbell-overhead-press.description: A standing barbell press that moves the bar from the upper chest to a stable overhead position.
instructions: Grip the bar just outside shoulder width, rest it at the upper chest, and stand tall with elbows slightly forward.
Press the bar vertically, moving your head back briefly so the bar can pass close to your face.
Finish with the bar over your midfoot, then lower it along the same close path to the upper chest.
Squeeze your glutes and keep your ribs down rather than arching your lower back to complete the press.

seated-barbell-shoulder-press.description: A seated barbell press that uses bench support for a steady shoulder-focused overhead drive.
instructions: Sit against an upright bench, grip the racked bar outside shoulder width, and unrack it to the upper chest.
Press the bar upward past your face while keeping your forearms beneath it.
Settle the bar over your shoulders at the top, then lower it under control to the starting point.
Maintain contact with the backrest and avoid flaring your ribs or bouncing the bar off your chest.

smith-machine-shoulder-press.description: A seated shoulder press that follows the guided vertical track of a Smith machine.
instructions: Center an upright bench under the bar, grip outside shoulder width, and unlock the bar at upper-chest height.
Press along the rails until your arms are straight while keeping your forearms aligned under the bar.
Pause at the top, then lower the bar steadily to just below chin level before the next repetition.
Position the bench so the track clears your face, and keep your back supported without excessive arching.

machine-shoulder-press.description: A guided seated press that loads the shoulders through the machine's fixed movement path.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles begin around shoulder height, then sit with your back on the pad.
Drive the handles upward until your arms are nearly straight, keeping your elbows under your hands.
Pause without locking hard at the top, then lower the handles slowly to the machine stops or start position.
Keep your head and torso against the pads and avoid shrugging your shoulders toward your ears.

arnold-press.description: A rotating dumbbell press that transitions from a palms-in front rack to an overhead finish.
instructions: Hold the dumbbells in front of your shoulders with palms facing you and elbows pointing forward.
Press upward while opening the elbows and rotating the palms to face forward.
Finish with the dumbbells overhead, then reverse the rotation as you lower to the front rack.
Rotate smoothly through the shoulders and keep your torso still rather than forcing the elbows far behind you.

single-arm-dumbbell-shoulder-press.description: A one-sided overhead press that challenges shoulder strength and resistance to trunk rotation.
instructions: Stand tall with one dumbbell at shoulder height, forearm vertical, and the free arm relaxed at your side.
Brace your trunk and press the dumbbell overhead without leaning toward the opposite side.
Stack the weight over that shoulder, then lower it smoothly back to the rack position before switching sides.
Keep both hips level and resist twisting or using your legs to start the press.

dumbbell-lateral-raise.description: A free-weight raise that trains the side shoulders by lifting the arms away from the body.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell at each side, palms inward, and elbows slightly bent.
Raise your arms out to the sides, leading with the elbows until they approach shoulder height.
Pause with the weights wide, then lower them slowly back beside your thighs.
Keep your torso quiet and wrists neutral instead of swinging or tipping the dumbbells upward.

cable-lateral-raise.description: A two-arm lateral raise that uses low cables for continuous tension across the side shoulders.
instructions: Stand centered between low pulleys, cross the cables, and hold the opposite handles near your thighs.
Lift both arms out to the sides with soft elbows until the handles approach shoulder height.
Hold the wide position briefly, then guide the crossed handles down without letting the stacks drop.
Stay upright and keep your shoulders away from your ears as the cables pull across your body.

single-arm-cable-lateral-raise.description: A unilateral low-cable raise that keeps steady tension on one side shoulder at a time.
instructions: Stand side-on to a low pulley, take the handle with the outside hand, and let the cable pass in front of you.
Raise the working arm out to the side with a soft elbow until it nears shoulder height.
Pause at the top, then lower the handle across the front of your body under control before changing sides.
Keep your hips square and avoid leaning away from the pulley to move the handle.

machine-lateral-raise.description: A guided lateral raise that places the upper arms against pads to focus work on the side shoulders.
instructions: Adjust the seat so your shoulder joints align with the machine pivots and place your upper arms against the pads.
Drive the pads outward and upward through your elbows until your upper arms approach shoulder height.
Pause at the raised position, then lower the pads slowly until they nearly meet the stops.
Keep your torso against the support and do not shrug or push through your hands.

dumbbell-front-raise.description: A dumbbell raise that emphasizes the front shoulders as the arms travel forward.
instructions: Stand with the dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms toward you, and elbows softly bent.
Raise the weights forward to about shoulder height without changing the elbow angle.
Pause in front, then lower the dumbbells to your thighs with a smooth, controlled descent.
Keep your ribs down and avoid rocking your torso or lifting the weights above a comfortable range.

cable-front-raise.description: A front shoulder raise using a low cable to maintain tension from the bottom of the arc.
instructions: Face away from a low pulley with the cable between your legs and hold its attachment in both hands in front of your thighs.
Raise the attachment forward with nearly straight arms until your hands reach shoulder height.
Pause at the front, then lower the attachment slowly until your arms return beside your thighs.
Stand tall and keep the cable from pulling your torso backward or your shoulders upward.

plate-front-raise.description: A two-handed plate raise that trains the front shoulders through a centered forward arc.
instructions: Stand tall and hold a weight plate securely at its sides in front of your thighs.
Lift the plate forward with softly bent elbows until its center reaches about shoulder height.
Hold the plate steady, then lower it under control to the front of your thighs.
Keep both hands firmly on the plate and avoid leaning back or using a hip swing.

dumbbell-rear-delt-fly.description: A hip-hinged dumbbell fly that trains the rear shoulders as the arms open away from the torso.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand, hinge forward with a flat back, and let your arms hang below your shoulders.
Sweep the dumbbells out to the sides with soft elbows until your upper arms align with your torso.
Pause in the open position, then lower the weights together beneath your chest slowly.
Maintain the same hinge and elbow angle, avoiding a torso rise or rowing motion.

face-pull.description: A rope cable pull toward the face that combines rear-shoulder movement with outward arm rotation.
instructions: Set a rope at upper-chest or face height, grasp both ends, and step back with arms extended.
Pull the rope toward your face while spreading its ends and driving your elbows outward.
Finish with your hands beside your temples, then extend your arms slowly toward the pulley.
Keep your ribs stacked and shoulders down instead of leaning back or jutting your head forward.

cable-external-rotation.description: A standing cable rotation that trains the shoulder while the upper arm stays anchored near the torso.
instructions: Stand side-on to a pulley set near elbow height and hold the handle with the far hand, elbow bent at your side.
Rotate your forearm away from the pulley while keeping your elbow pinned near your ribs.
Stop before the upper arm shifts, then guide the handle back across your abdomen slowly.
Keep your wrist straight and torso square so the movement comes from shoulder rotation, not body turning.

resistance-band-external-rotation.description: A band-resisted shoulder rotation performed with the elbow held close to the side.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band near elbow height, stand side-on, and take it in the outside hand with your elbow bent.
Rotate the forearm outward against the band while the upper arm remains beside your ribs.
Pause at your controlled outer range, then return the hand toward your abdomen without losing band tension.
Keep your shoulder down, wrist neutral, and torso still rather than twisting away from the anchor.

dumbbell-external-rotation.description: A side-lying dumbbell rotation that isolates the shoulder with the upper arm supported by the torso.
instructions: Lie on your side with the top elbow bent against your ribs and hold a dumbbell across your abdomen.
Keeping the elbow fixed, rotate the forearm upward until it points near vertical or reaches a comfortable limit.
Pause at the top, then lower the dumbbell across your abdomen with control before changing sides.
Do not roll your torso backward or let the elbow drift away from your side.

upright-row.description: A close-to-body barbell pull that trains the shoulders as the elbows rise outward.
instructions: Stand with the bar in front of your thighs using an overhand grip and arms extended.
Pull the bar upward close to your torso, leading with your elbows as they move out to the sides.
Stop at a comfortable height below the point where your shoulders roll forward, then lower the bar slowly.
Keep your wrists aligned with your forearms and avoid leaning back or jerking the bar upward.

cable-upright-row.description: An upright row using a low cable for a smooth, continuously resisted shoulder pull.
instructions: Face a low pulley, hold a straight-bar attachment overhand, and stand with the cable centered between your feet.
Draw the bar up along your torso by lifting your elbows outward and keeping your hands below them.
End at a comfortable upper range, then guide the attachment down until your arms are straight.
Stay tall and keep the pull smooth rather than shrugging, rocking, or forcing your elbows higher.

dumbbell-upright-row.description: A two-dumbbell upright pull that allows each shoulder and wrist to follow its own path.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, palms facing your body.
Pull the dumbbells upward near your sides while your elbows travel out and above your hands.
Stop within a comfortable shoulder range, then lower both dumbbells steadily to your thighs.
Let the weights separate naturally and avoid swinging your torso or forcing the elbows high.

landmine-press.description: An angled two-handed barbell press that drives the landmine end forward and upward from the chest.
instructions: Face the landmine, cup the end of the bar with both hands at your upper chest, and take a stable stance.
Press the bar away and upward along its arc while keeping your torso square to the anchor.
Finish with both arms extended toward the bar path, then draw the bar back to your chest under control.
Keep your ribs down and do not turn the movement into a standing incline press by leaning into the bar.

single-arm-landmine-press.description: A one-arm angled barbell press that trains the shoulder while the trunk resists rotation.
instructions: Face the landmine in a staggered stance and hold the bar end at one shoulder with your palm underneath it.
Press the bar forward and upward along its arc as you keep your chest facing the anchor.
Reach fully through the press, then lower the bar end smoothly back to the same shoulder before switching arms.
Keep your wrist stacked under the bar and resist twisting, side-bending, or driving with your legs.

kettlebell-halo.description: A controlled kettlebell circle around the head that moves the shoulders through multiple angles.
instructions: Stand tall and hold the kettlebell by the horn sides upside down in front of your upper chest.
Guide the bell around one side of your head, behind it, and forward around the other side in a close circle.
Finish with the bell centered at your chest, then repeat the circle in the opposite direction.
Keep your head still, ribs down, and elbows controlled so the bell clears your head without contacting it.
